# Equal outer section mass and the middle chord displacement bound

This is a geometric consequence of FULL joint cap-parameter stationarity,
not merely of the middle body equations. It applies to three positive
planar convex fibers K0,K1,K2 with (K0+K2)/2 contained in K1.

## 1. The exact stationarity hypothesis

Consider a full-rank three-cap middle circuit through (1,y), where y is an
interior deepest point of K1. Give each deepest endpoint its own isolating
critical circuit and each nondeep fiber its own slack circuit. Thus the
middle group is assigned ONLY the index1 in its whole-fiber cover constraint.
This is a valid finite cover irrespective of the middle projected circuit
normal: each group covers its own entire fiber. There are at most two groups
with positive budget multipliers because both endpoints cannot be deepest.

Assume the normalized joint stress exists under the cap motions described in
candidate 5e600a897e2488c6 and rotating-circuit-section-centroids.md.
Body compatibility multipliers do not enter cap-coordinate derivatives.
For every middle cap with a positive multiplier, threshold and integer-normal
variation therefore give total effective section integer mean exactly1.
The full-rank continuous-normal circuit variations give one common effective
full section centroid. Its integer coordinate is1; since it belongs to all
three cap planes through (1,y), its continuous coordinate is y.

In particular, for EACH such cap its effective section measure has mean
(1,y). These are precisely the hypotheses needed below. The conclusion can
also be read as an independent lemma assuming these means directly, without
assuming an extremizer or a stress construction.

## 2. Effective subdensities and an elementary interval fact

Normalize the continuous cap normal to unit length. Its section in K1 is a
proper chord J1 of length L>0, with ordinary uniform length density. In an
endpoint fiber the effective section is a density theta_e in [0,1] on the
actual chord Je. A transverse section has theta_e=1; a cap/body supporting
coincidence may have any measurable theta_e permitted by the stress. Thus no
boundary coincidence is discarded.

If a density theta in [0,1] on an interval [a,b] has mass s>0 and mean c,
then

    [c-s/2,c+s/2] is contained in [a,b].                       (1)

Indeed, putting F(t)=integral_a^(a+t) theta, one has F(t)<=t and

    integral (x-a)theta(x) dx
       =integral_0^(b-a) [s-F(t)] dt >= integral_0^s(s-t)dt=s^2/2.

Hence c>=a+s/2; reflect the interval for the other inequality.

## 3. Midpoint compatibility controls the displacement

Let s0,s2 be the effective endpoint section masses. Integer mean1 gives

    s0=s2=s.                                                (2)

If s=0, the total continuous mean condition immediately says the middle
chord midpoint c1 equals y. Suppose s>0, and let c0,c2 be the endpoint
effective section means. By (1), a uniform segment of length s centered at
ce lies in Je. Their Minkowski average is therefore a segment of length s
centered at q=(c0+c2)/2 inside J1: convexity puts it in K1 and the affine
cap equation puts it on the middle cap boundary. Consequently

    0<s<=L,       |q-c1| <= (L-s)/2.                         (3)

Here all differences are along the common chord direction; Euclidean
lengths are used. The full continuous section mean condition is

    y=(L c1+2s q)/(L+2s).

Writing r=s/L in [0,1], this proves the exact bound

    |c1-y|/(L/2) <= 2r(1-r)/(1+2r) <= 2-sqrt(3).             (4)

For the last inequality, its difference after multiplying by 1+2r is

    2 [r-(sqrt(3)-1)/2]^2 >=0.

Thus every cap chord in this fully transported middle circuit passes
within a fraction 2-sqrt(3) of its half-length from its midpoint.

More precisely, if delta=|c1-y|/(L/2), then its outer-to-middle section
mass ratio must satisfy

    2r^2-2(1-delta)r+delta <=0,
    [(1-delta)-sqrt(1-4delta+delta^2)]/2 <= r
      <= [(1-delta)+sqrt(1-4delta+delta^2)]/2.                 (5)

The cap multiplier relation still includes this ratio exactly:
lambda_j L_j(1+2r_j)=rho_j t. Therefore (4) should not be used as a
replacement for the actual shared t, rho, and cap-budget conditions.

## 4. Audit boundary and an exclusion

The central-only example in candidate fb44ce6857cb7961 has its
third cap anchor at parameter13/20 of that chord. Its relative midpoint
displacement is3/10, larger than2-sqrt(3), since (17/10)^2<3. Thus that
example cannot extend to the full mean-transport configuration of this note.
It is a counterexample to the plain signed-centroid profile step only.

The full-rank hypothesis is material. For a rank-one two-cap circuit, common
plane membership leaves the tangential component of the transported centroid
undetermined; this note does not identify it with the originally selected
center. Nor does this note itself prove a cap multiplier or OC bound.
